speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the exact location of your wrist pain and when it started. Did you experience any trauma or injury prior to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To differentiate between de Quervain's tenosynovitis, a TFCC injury from your fall, or early inflammatory arthritis, have you noticed any specific pain when tilting your wrist side-to-side or gripping objects tightly?

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand ibuprofen has been helpful; does the pain specifically worsen when you make a fist or when someone gently presses on the tendons at the base of your thumb? Additionally, have you noticed any morning stiffness that lasts longer than 30 minutes?

REQUEST TEST: Phalen's test, Finkelstein's test, and grip strength assessment.
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of right first dorsal compartment.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Phalen's Test: Not reported; Finkelstein's Test: Positive, eliciting pain on the radial side of the wrist when grasping the thumb and exerting longitudinal traction towards the ulnar side; Grip Strength Assessment: Not reported. Ultrasound of right first dorsal compartment: Not performed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The positive Finkelstein test and pain on thumb abduction confirm inflammation of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis tendons at the first dorsal compartment. Given the three-month duration and lack of significant morning stiffness, rheumatoid arthritis is unlikely despite your family history. I recommend continuing NSAIDs and initiating a thumb spica splint for immobilization and rest.
